{
  "candidate_rtl": "module pw_alu #(
    parameter WIDTH = 64
)(
    input wire [WIDTH-1:0] a, b,
    input wire [2:0] Oper,
    output reg [WIDTH-1:0] sum
);
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] x;
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] add_c, ab_c, ba_c;
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] add_p, add_g, ab_p, ab_g, ba_p, ba_g;
    wire s_add, s_ab, s_ba, s_or, s_and, s_xor, s_xnor;

    assign x = a ^ b;
    assign add_p = a | b;
    assign add_g = a & b;
    assign ab_p = ~a | b;
    assign ab_g = ~a & b;
    assign ba_p = a | ~b;
    assign ba_g = a & ~b;

    pw_alu_carry4 #(.WIDTH(WIDTH)) u_add (
        .p(add_p), .g(add_g), .c(add_c)
    );
    pw_alu_carry4 #(.WIDTH(WIDTH)) u_ab (
        .p(ab_p), .g(ab_g), .c(ab_c)
    );
    pw_alu_carry4 #(.WIDTH(WIDTH)) u_ba (
        .p(ba_p), .g(ba_g), .c(ba_c)
    );

    assign s_add  = (Oper == 3'b000);
    assign s_ab   = (Oper == 3'b001);
    assign s_ba   = (Oper == 3'b010);
    assign s_or   = (Oper == 3'b011);
    assign s_and  = (Oper == 3'b100);
    assign s_xor  = (Oper == 3'b101);
    assign s_xnor = (Oper == 3'b110);

    always @* begin
        sum = ({WIDTH{s_add}}  & (x ^ add_c))
            | ({WIDTH{s_ab}}   & (x ^ ab_c))
            | ({WIDTH{s_ba}}   & (x ^ ba_c))
            | ({WIDTH{s_or}}   & (a | b))
            | ({WIDTH{s_and}}  & (a & b))
            | ({WIDTH{s_xor}}  & x)
            | ({WIDTH{s_xnor}} & ~x);
    end
endmodule

module pw_alu_carry4 #(
    parameter WIDTH = 64
)(
    input wire [WIDTH-1:0] p,
    input wire [WIDTH-1:0] g,
    output wire [WIDTH-1:0] c
);
    function integer levels4;
        input integer n;
        integer v;
        begin
            v = n;
            levels4 = 0;
            while (v > 1) begin
                v = (v + 3) / 4;
                levels4 = levels4 + 1;
            end
        end
    endfunction

    localparam integer NG = (WIDTH + 3) / 4;
    localparam integer PAD = 4 * NG;
    localparam integer NL = levels4(NG);
    wire [PAD-1:0] bp, bg;
    wire [NG-1:0] pp [0:NL];
    wire [NG-1:0] gg [0:NL];
    wire [NG-1:0] boundary;

    genvar i, j, l;
    generate
        for (i = 0; i < PAD; i = i + 1) begin: bits_pad
            if (i < WIDTH) begin: real_bit
                assign bp[i] = p[i];
                assign bg[i] = g[i];
            end else begin: pad_bit
                assign bp[i] = 1'b1;
                assign bg[i] = 1'b0;
            end
        end

        for (j = 0; j < NG; j = j + 1) begin: groups
            assign pp[0][j] = bp[4*j+3] & bp[4*j+2]
                            & bp[4*j+1] & bp[4*j];
            assign gg[0][j] = bg[4*j+3]
                            | (bp[4*j+3] & bg[4*j+2])
                            | (bp[4*j+3] & bp[4*j+2] & bg[4*j+1])
                            | (bp[4*j+3] & bp[4*j+2] & bp[4*j+1] & bg[4*j]);
            if (j == 0) begin: first_group
                assign boundary[j] = 1'b0;
            end else begin: later_group
                assign boundary[j] = gg[NL][j-1];
            end
        end

        for (l = 0; l < NL; l = l + 1) begin: prefix_level
            localparam integer D = 4 ** l;
            for (j = 0; j < NG; j = j + 1) begin: prefix_group
                if (j >= 3*D) begin: four
                    assign pp[l+1][j] = pp[l][j] & pp[l][j-D]
                                       & pp[l][j-2*D] & pp[l][j-3*D];
                    assign gg[l+1][j] = gg[l][j]
                        | (pp[l][j] & gg[l][j-D])
                        | (pp[l][j] & pp[l][j-D] & gg[l][j-2*D])
                        | (pp[l][j] & pp[l][j-D] & pp[l][j-2*D] & gg[l][j-3*D]);
                end else if (j >= 2*D) begin: three
                    assign pp[l+1][j] = pp[l][j] & pp[l][j-D] & pp[l][j-2*D];
                    assign gg[l+1][j] = gg[l][j]
                        | (pp[l][j] & gg[l][j-D])
                        | (pp[l][j] & pp[l][j-D] & gg[l][j-2*D]);
                end else if (j >= D) begin: two
                    assign pp[l+1][j] = pp[l][j] & pp[l][j-D];
                    assign gg[l+1][j] = gg[l][j] | (pp[l][j] & gg[l][j-D]);
                end else begin: one
                    assign pp[l+1][j] = pp[l][j];
                    assign gg[l+1][j] = gg[l][j];
                end
            end
        end

        for (i = 0; i < WIDTH; i = i + 1) begin: local_carry
            if ((i % 4) == 0) begin: offset0
                assign c[i] = boundary[i/4];
            end else if ((i % 4) == 1) begin: offset1
                assign c[i] = bg[i-1] | (bp[i-1] & boundary[i/4]);
            end else if ((i % 4) == 2) begin: offset2
                assign c[i] = bg[i-1]
                    | (bp[i-1] & bg[i-2])
                    | (bp[i-1] & bp[i-2] & boundary[i/4]);
            end else begin: offset3
                assign c[i] = bg[i-1]
                    | (bp[i-1] & bg[i-2])
                    | (bp[i-1] & bp[i-2] & bg[i-3])
                    | (bp[i-1] & bp[i-2] & bp[i-3] & boundary[i/4]);
            end
        end
    endgenerate
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The baseline critical paths traverse long arithmetic carry/borrow cones before the final operation selection. The reported worst arrival is 3.00 ns, with paths extending from low-order operand bits to high-order result bits.",
  "rewrite": "Compute addition and both subtraction directions concurrently using explicit sparse radix-4 carry/borrow lookahead. Four-bit group summaries feed two radix-4 group-prefix levels at WIDTH=64, followed by local lookahead. OR-based propagate terms avoid an initial XOR on the carry paths. A shared operand XOR produces arithmetic result bits, and one-hot operation masks select the final result without putting operation decoding ahead of the arithmetic networks.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected to reduce arithmetic depth and improve on the 3.00 ns baseline. A reasonable target is approximately 2.3–2.7 ns, but this is an unmeasured estimate; the specified mapping, STA, and electrical checks must establish the actual result.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Three parallel arithmetic lookahead networks trade area for timing and avoid an operand-selection stage. Sparse four-bit grouping limits prefix wiring and duplicated logic. The design is intended to fit the 13121.834880 um2 cap, but mapped area and electrical compliance have not been measured.",
  "functional_boundaries": "All seven binary operation encodings retain their original unsigned WIDTH-bit results; Oper=111 produces zero. Addition and subtraction wrap modulo 2^WIDTH. Subtraction uses exact borrow recurrences with zero initial borrow, including the reverse-operand operation. The module name, ports, output-reg declaration, and WIDTH parameter are preserved. Positive widths, including nonmultiples of four, are handled by identity padding. The design is entirely combinational and introduces no state, latency, assumptions, assertions, or undefined outputs."
}
